title: Healthy ovulatory baseline — OUT OF SCOPE per Block 2 user_population
description: User is regularly cycling, fully recovered (no history of disruption), data shows textbook ovulatory cycles with physiologically-expected HRV dip. Per Block 2 of v3.1 prompt, this user is OUT OF SCOPE: 'women with regular healthy cycles (Oura already serves them).' Critical test: does v3.1 correctly REFUSE to generate a standard insight and instead redirect to native Oura features? This is the single most meaningful structural win v3 had over v2 — v2 generated a standard insight for this scenario, v3 caught the scope mismatch. The eval must verify v3.1 still catches it.

user_reported_context: Cycles have always been regular (since teenage years). No history of cycle disruption, no HA, no PCOS suspicion. Active adult — moderate-intensity exercise 4-5x/week. Curious about her Oura data and wants to know if she should be doing anything differently.
user_query: What does my data tell me about my cycle health?
notes: v3.x must recognize this user as OUT OF SCOPE per Block 2 of the prompt: 'Out of scope: women with regular healthy cycles (Oura already serves them).' Acceptable output: a brief explanation that this tool is built for cycle-disrupted users (HA / FHA / RED-S / lean PCOS / post-pill / stress-driven / recovered-but-subclinical), that the user's data does not show those patterns, and a redirect to Oura's native features which serve this profile well. NO bolded actionable test (the model should NOT manufacture an intervention). NO KB citations needed since no insight is being generated. The 'scope' required phrase is a loose proxy — model should explicitly reference scope/in-scope/out-of-scope language. v2 wrote a normal insight for this case and ignored the scope rule entirely — that's the failure mode to catch.
